_directive: losslessly compressed, token-efficient, information-dense, fully detailed, machine-facing; optimized for model parsing over human readability
question: What factor actually controls KB output size/depth: input grain, or the density-mode budget? Does decomposing a domain into subdomains add real coverage?
method: Hold DENSITY_MODE=dense constant; vary INPUT GRAIN. Compare one domain-grain KB (IR whole) vs three subdomain-grain KBs (IR ranking / indexing / neural). Gate every run.

domain_grain.label: run1_ir
domain_grain.node_character: coarse: each node = a whole IR area (e.g. 'lexical retrieval', 'evaluation')

subdomain_grain.label: runS1_ir_ranking
subdomain_grain.node_character: fine: each node = one mechanism (BM25 k1, BM25 b, BM25F, JM/Dirichlet smoothing, LambdaMART, IPS debias, MMR)

subdomain_grain.label: runS2_ir_indexing
subdomain_grain.node_character: fine: each node = one structure/method (PForDelta postings, skip pointers, SPIMI, wavelet tree)

subdomain_grain.label: runS3_ir_neural
subdomain_grain.node_character: fine: each node = one work unit (DPR bi-encoder, ColBERT, HNSW/PQ, hard-neg mining, RRF, HyDE, RAG, BEIR)

aggregate_comparison.coverage_gain: 3.1x nodes, 2.5x tokens for 3x the runs; all gate-passing
aggregate_comparison.per_kb_node_budget: 19-20 at BOTH grains (dense target 19-24) -> budget is INVARIANT to grain

factor_analysis.controlling_factor: the density-mode object budget PER RUN (dense=19-24 nodes / 32-40 edges). It is fixed regardless of how broad or narrow the input scope is.
factor_analysis.role_of_grain: input grain does NOT change how much one KB produces; it sets the RESOLUTION of the fixed budget (what each node represents).
factor_analysis.batching_up_effect: more scope in one KB (e.g. 2 domains) -> same fixed budget spread thinner -> per-topic depth DROPS (prior run: IR 19->8 nodes).
factor_analysis.breaking_down_effect: less scope per KB (subdomain) -> same fixed budget at finer resolution -> per-topic depth RISES; TOTAL coverage = (#KBs) x (budget).

secondary_factors.density_mode: the PRIMARY knob for per-run budget; change mode (compact/standard/dense) to change how much one run yields, NOT scope.
secondary_factors.semantic_richness: drives tok/node (observed 1226-2032) and thus total tokens, but NOT node count.
secondary_factors.output_ceiling: max single KB seen = 40648 tokens, no truncation; practical upper band ~40-45k. Units richer than that must be split or use a lighter mode.

scaling_law: Coverage is multiplied by RECURSIVE DECOMPOSITION + FAN-OUT, not by batch size. Choose grain so each unit is rich enough to justify a full dense budget yet small enough to fit one response (<~40k tok). Generate one dense KB per unit; fan out in parallel; gate + commit each.

revised_decision.unit_of_generation: ONE taxonomy node at SUBDOMAIN (or field) grain per dense KB
revised_decision.rationale: domain grain lumps mechanisms into single nodes and loses detail (BM25 became 1 node); subdomain grain captured the same area as ~20 mechanism-level nodes and still passed the gate.
revised_decision.recommended_grain: subdomain/field level for high-value areas; drop to standard/compact for narrow/low-value units; split further only if a unit would exceed ~40k tokens at dense
revised_decision.knowledge_searcher_implication: do NOT generate 8 domain KBs; generate ~1 dense KB per subdomain across the seed taxonomy (~24 subdomains -> ~24 dense KBs, ~480-570 fine-grained nodes total) as the foundational Knowledge Searcher KB set
revised_decision.concurrency: 3-6 helpers in parallel observed stable (~10-15 min each)
